To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

NMOSD and especially MOG ON are important differential diagnosis of MS associated ON and idiopathic autoimmune ON; that the prognosis of both entities is good, if treated early and aggressively; and that, in the case of NMOSD, eculizumad is the first approved treatment for relapsing disease.

NMOSD is a relapsing autoimmune disease that can be associated with ON, myelitis, brainstem encephelitis and other clinical manifestations; MOG associated encephalitis can also be associated with ON; both NMOSD and myelin oligdendrocyte associated disorders can be associated with brain lesions on MRI; NMOSD and MS are not the same disease; NMOSD is an autoimmune disease and not an inflammatory disease; the treatment of NMOS
NMOSD and the newly described entity of MOG EM are both important differential diagnoses of MS associated and "idiopathic" ON.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: 1) the clinical presentation of NMOSD ON (including the frequency of simultaneous or consecutive attacks in other regions of the CNS) 2) the clinical presentation and outcome of MOG ON 3) the efficacy of rituximab for MOG ON 4) the efficacy of PEX/ IA for MOG ON.
the diagnosis and treatment in patients with AQP4 antibody and MOG antibody associated ON.
the development of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of diseases of the central and peripheral nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

both NMOSD ON as well as MOG ON should be considered as possible diagnoses in all cases of acute ON, especially if there are atypical features (e.g. bilateral ON, simultaneous or consecutive myelitis, brainstem encephalis, supratentoral MRI brain lesions) or if there is an incomplete response to steroids and PEX/IA.

both NMOSD and AQP4 antibody associated ON as well as MOG EM and MOG ON have been shown to be different entities from MS and that the clinical presentation and treatment response of MOG EM and ON is distinct from that of NMOSD.

NMOSD and especially MOG ON are not only rare, but also very important differential diagnosis of both MS-associated ON and idiopathic autoimmune ON, and should be considered in all patients presenting with ON, especially in the presence of atypical clinical or MRI features, and if a relapsing disease course is suspected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diagnosis of NMOSD and, especially, MOG EM is often missed and that both diseases are often treated with ineffective or even harmful therapies.
both NMOSD ON as well as MOG ON can lead to severe visual impairment or blindness and that the prognosis of both entities is better than previously assumed.

the diagnosis and treatment options of both NMOSD ON (also known as Devic's disease) and MOG ON (also known under the umbrella term "chronic relapse inflammatory optic neuropathy") have been significantly improved in recent years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both NMOSD ON as well as MOG EM ON should be considered in every patient presenting with acute or relapsing optic neuritis.
both NMOSD and, especially, MOG ON should be considered in the differential diagnosis of any patient presenting with an acute or subacute onset of ON.
both NMOSD ON und MOG EM should be considered as differential diagnoses in any patient presenting with ON, even if the MRI is suggestive of MS.
